The idea

A design token is a name for a design decision. The name says what the value is for, and the design system holds the value.

  • A name, not a value

    You pick “the muted text colour”, not #6e6e6e. The name stays right when the colour changes.

  • One source

    The website, the docs and the blog read the same tokens. A change made here reaches each of them with the next version.

  • Checked for you

    Every text colour is measured against its background in both themes. A command reports a value typed by hand.

What do you need?

  • I choose colours, type or spacingRead Colour, Type, Spacing and Shape. Click a name to copy it.

  • I am looking for one tokenThe Tokens page lists every token and filters by name or use.

Colour

A colour is named for its job: text, a background, an action, a line or a message. Choose by the job, never by the nearest shade. Each one has a value for the light theme and one for the dark theme, and switches by itself.

Text

Four strengths of text. Body copy never goes lighter than muted.

  • Aa

    Headlines.

  • Aa

    Strong text and the default text of a page.

  • Aa

    Body copy and the paragraph under a heading.

  • Aa

    Captions, card descriptions and small labels.

Backgrounds

The page, a band that alternates with it, a card, a soft tint and the one dark surface.

  • The page background.

  • A section band that alternates with the page.

  • The fill of a card.

  • A soft tint behind a chip or a callout.

  • The one dark surface, such as a table header.

Buttons and links

One action colour. A filled button uses the fill and its label; a link or an outline uses the text colour.

  • The fill of the main button.

  • The label on that fill.

  • A link, an outline button label, an eyebrow.

  • The fill of the main button under the pointer.

Lines

Borders of cards, dividers and form fields.

  • The border of a card or a chip.

  • A quiet divider.

  • The border of a form field.

Messages

Error, success, warning and information. Each has a text colour and a tinted background.

  • An error message.

  • A confirmation.

  • A warning.

  • A note or a tip.

Type

15 text styles, each named for its role on the page. Put the class on the element and the font, size, weight and line height come with it. The numbers show the size on this screen right now.

Shape

Corners and shadows are named by what they sit on. A card takes the card radius; a button is always a pill.

Corners

  • OSS tag and checkbox.

  • Small elements and the monogram badge.

  • Icon tiles, stat badges and nav link rows.

  • Marketing cards and media frames.

  • Emphasis and catalog cards.

  • Pills: every action, chip and framework selector.

Shadows

  • Card hover: cards lift shadow only, no translate or scale.

  • Floating stat badges.

  • Dropdown menus and popovers.

  • Open nav panel.

Themes and dials

The same component looks right in the light theme, in the dark theme and at any density, because it reads tokens. Nothing in it is written twice.

Dials

Four dials change every token below them at once. Press a value and watch the card: its padding, corners and shadow follow, and no rule of the card changes.

Size --ig-size
Spacing --ig-spacing
Roundness --ig-radius-factor
Shadow --ig-elevation-factor

A site sets a dial once, on the page or on one region. A component never sets one.

Build a component

The same four steps in plain HTML, Astro, React, Angular or a web component.

  1. Mark the root. Put data-ig-scope on the outermost element of the component. A dial set anywhere above it then reaches it.
  2. Colour by job. Text reads a color-text-* token, a background a color-surface-* token, a line a color-border-* token.
  3. Space by role. Padding is space-inset-*, a vertical margin space-stack-*, a gap space-gap-*.
  4. Set text with a class. igd-type-title-sm on a card title, igd-type-body-md on its text.

This is the whole stylesheet of the card used on this page:

.card {
  display: grid;
  gap: var(--igd-space-gap-sm);
  padding: var(--igd-space-inset-lg);
  border: var(--igd-border-width-default) solid var(--igd-color-border-default);
  border-radius: var(--igd-radius-lg);
  background: var(--igd-color-surface-card);
  color: var(--igd-color-text-secondary);
  box-shadow: var(--igd-shadow-raised);
}
<article class="card" data-ig-scope>
  <h3 class="igd-type-title-sm">Card title</h3>
  <p class="igd-type-body-md">Card text.</p>
</article>

Do and don't

Six rules cover almost every case. The check command reports the first three; the third with --strict.

  • Docolor: var(--igd-color-text-muted);
    Don'tcolor: var(--ig-gray-600);

    Read a colour by its job. A palette step such as --ig-gray-600 is raw material for the design system and has no dark value of its own.

  • Dopadding: var(--igd-space-inset-md);
    Don'tpadding: var(--igd-space-md);

    Use a spacing role, not the raw step. The role says what the space is, so padding and gaps can be tuned apart later.

  • Docolor: var(--igd-color-action-text);
    Don'tcolor: #1a5fff;

    Do not type a colour, even one that looks right. When no token fits, say which one is missing.

  • Dobackground: var(--igd-color-surface-card);
    Don'tbackground: light-dark(#fff, #1c1c1c);

    A token already has a value per theme. Do not write the two themes by hand.

  • Do<section style="--ig-spacing: 0.5">
    Don't.card { --igd-space-md: 8px; }

    Change a dial on the page or on a region. Never set a spacing, size or radius step inside a component.

  • Domax-width: 24rem;
    Don'tmax-width: var(--igd-space-6xl);

    Widths, heights and offsets are not tokens. Type them; do not borrow a spacing step for a size.

Set up a site

For the developer who adds the design system to a site. It is CSS only: no framework code and no dependencies.

  1. Install the package.
    npm install ig-design-system
  2. Load the stylesheets before the site's own styles, in this order. fonts.css and base.css are optional.
    @import 'ig-design-system/fonts.css';
@import 'ig-design-system/tokens.css';
@import 'ig-design-system/theme.css';
@import 'ig-design-system/base.css';
  3. Check the site. The command reports an unknown token, a palette step and a raw spacing step, and fails the build when it finds one.
    npx ig-design-system check src

Something missing?

If no token fits what you need, do not pick the closest one. Ask: the answer is either a token you missed or a new one for everybody.

  • Search the tokens firstThe filter matches a token's name and its use, so hover or card work.
  • Open an issueSay what you are styling and which token is missing.
  • The repositoryThe source, the README and the reason behind every decision.
